message:
Please review the following document.

<document>
Grant Application: Chilled Storage for Fresh Food Distribution
Applicant: Hollins Valley Food Bank (registered charity)
To: Ashworth Community Foundation, Community Resilience Fund (capital grants)
Amount requested: £48,600

1. About us
Hollins Valley Food Bank has provided emergency food to households in the valley since 2014. We are run by two part-time paid staff and around 70 volunteers, and we operate from a warehouse in Hollinsford and three distribution sites in Hollinsford, Brackley Bridge and Over Hollins, which open on different days of the week. Referrals come from GPs, schools, Citizens Advice and the local authority's welfare team.

2. The need
Demand has risen sharply. The number of households we supported rose from an average of 410 a week in 2023 to 620 a week in 2025, an increase of 66%. Over the same period our food donations have changed in character. Supermarket surplus schemes now offer us large volumes of fresh produce, dairy and chilled ready meals, but we have no chilled storage beyond three domestic fridges, so we currently decline around 1.2 tonnes of fresh food each week. Our parcels are therefore dominated by tinned and dried goods, and clients, referrers and our own volunteers consistently tell us that families want fresh food, particularly for children.

3. The project
We are seeking funding to:
- install a 12 cubic metre walk-in cold room at our Hollinsford warehouse;
- buy a used refrigerated van, so that chilled food can be collected from supermarket depots and taken to our four distribution sites at safe temperatures;
- upgrade the warehouse electrical supply to support the cold room.

With these in place we could accept the 1.2 tonnes a week we currently decline, about 62 tonnes a year. Using the national food-redistribution conversion of 2,380 meals per tonne, that is around 147,600 additional meals a year, at a one-off capital cost of about 33p per meal in the first year alone.

4. Budget
Item | Cost
Walk-in cold room, supply and installation | £26,400
Refrigerated van (three years old, 40,000 miles) | £18,500
Electrical supply upgrade | £3,700
Total requested | £48,600

Quotes from two suppliers were obtained for the cold room and the electrical work; the lower quote is shown in each case. The van price is from a commercial dealer and includes a 12-month warranty.

5. Running costs
We have obtained estimates for the additional running costs. The cold room will add around £4,200 a year to our electricity bill. Insurance, fuel, servicing and road tax for the van will cost around £6,800 a year. Our 2025 accounts show total income of £96,000, almost all of it restricted to food purchasing and staff costs, an unrestricted surplus of £900, and unrestricted reserves of £5,100.

6. Outcomes and monitoring
We will measure:
- tonnes of fresh and chilled food received and distributed each month;
- the proportion of parcels containing fresh produce (currently under 10%; target 80% within six months);
- client feedback through our quarterly survey.
We will report to the Foundation at six and twelve months.

7. Timetable
The cold room supplier can install within eight weeks of order. We would order on award, with the cold room and van in service by October 2026.

8. Sustainability
This is a one-off capital investment. Once installed, the cold room and van will be sustainable without further grant funding, and will serve the valley for at least ten years. Our partner supermarkets have confirmed in writing that they will continue to offer us surplus fresh food.

9. Why fund us
The Foundation's Community Resilience Fund aims to strengthen local organisations' long-term capacity to meet need. This project does exactly that: a modest capital investment that permanently transforms the quality of the food we can give to families, at a very low cost per meal.
</document>
response:
# Review of the grant application

The application is clear and well structured, but one statistic is wrong and the sustainability claim is contradicted by the applicant's own figures. A funder would likely notice both.

## Errors to fix

1. **The demand increase is miscalculated (Section 2).** Going from 410 to 620 households a week is a rise of 210/410, or **51%**, not 66%. Correct it, because a funder checking the arithmetic will doubt the other figures too.

2. **The timetable has already passed (Section 7).** The application targets "in service by October 2026", but that date is now behind us. Either the application predates today and needs a new date, or the timeline needs rebasing. Eight weeks from order, plus time for the van and electrical work, should be reflected in a realistic date.

3. **The number of distribution sites is inconsistent.** Section 1 lists three distribution sites (Hollinsford, Brackley Bridge, Over Hollins), but Section 3 refers to "our four distribution sites". If the warehouse counts as the fourth, say so.

## The main weakness: sustainability vs. running costs

- Section 5 puts the new running costs at **£11,000 a year** (£4,200 electricity plus £6,800 van).
- The same section shows an unrestricted surplus of **£900** and unrestricted reserves of **£5,100**, with nearly all income restricted to food purchasing and staff.
- Reserves would cover less than six months of the new costs.
- Section 8 nonetheless says the equipment "will be sustainable without further grant funding", and Section 9 says it builds "long-term capacity". The application's own numbers contradict both statements.

The application should include a funding plan for the £11,000, such as:
- a request for 2–3 years of running costs in the grant
- pledged support from partner supermarkets
- a new fundraising line or sponsorship
- a contribution from referrers or the local authority

It should also cover costs not yet mentioned: maintenance and repair of the cold room, van MOT and breakdown cover after the 12-month warranty, and who will drive the van and how they will be insured and trained.

## Cost-per-meal claim

The 33p figure is arithmetically right (£48,600 ÷ 147,600) but misleading. It counts only the capital cost and excludes running costs. Including the first year's £11,000 gives about **40p**, and the figure keeps rising over the ten-year life. Present both, or label it clearly as "capital cost only". Also cite the source of the 2,380 meals/tonne conversion (e.g. WRAP). Note that 1.2 t × 52 weeks is 62.4 tonnes, so the 62-tonne figure is a slight rounding down, which is fine.

## Smaller points

- **The van has only one quote.** Section 4 says two quotes were obtained for the cold room and electrical work. The van comes from one dealer, so add a comparison or a short justification.
- **Food safety is missing.** Say who is responsible for temperature monitoring, HACCP or food hygiene registration, and the volunteer training that handling chilled food requires. Funders of cold-chain projects usually look for this.
- **The 80% target needs support.** Going from under 10% to 80% of parcels containing fresh produce in six months is ambitious. 1.2 t a week across about 620 households is roughly 2 kg each. Show how this works across the four sites and how quickly you can ramp up.
- **Evidence for the supermarket commitments.** The application says they are "confirmed in writing", so attach the letters. Check whether they guarantee volumes or only goodwill.
- **Asset lifespan.** "At least ten years" is plausible for the cold room, but less so for a used van with 40,000 miles. Consider a separate replacement or depreciation note.
- **Section 9 is the weakest section.** It restates the funder's aims without evidence. Tie it to specific outcomes, such as tonnes diverted from waste, households reached, and health benefits for children.

## Suggested priority

1. Fix the 66% figure to 51%.
2. Update the timetable.
3. Add a credible plan for the £11,000 a year in running costs, and revise Sections 8 and 9 to match.
4. Restate the cost-per-meal figure with running costs included.
5. Resolve the site-count inconsistency and add the food safety and van-driver details.

I can draft revised wording for Sections 5, 8 and 9 if you'd like.
